subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & cost levers — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@orionai.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciate the clarity on your user experience goals. Quick recap of the SLOs and open items so we all have the same picture: 

SLOs discussed:
- Token-level streaming latency: target ~200ms p95 token latency for streaming responses (progressively rendered to UI).
- End-to-end single-turn latency: target <= 400ms p95 for 60-token responses (non-streaming fallback).
- Concurrency: sustain ~50 concurrent live sessions during peak, with burst to 100 for short spikes.
- Throughput: ~300 requests/minute sustained, average response length ~60 tokens.

Primary constraints you highlighted:
- Must keep per-token cost under your current threshold (target: ~30% cheaper than your current vendor).
- Streaming must start delivering tokens within 150-250ms to preserve UX.
- Some inputs require long-context support (up to 8k tokens) for thread history.

Suggested cost/performance levers (we'll follow up with numbers and a small benchmark):
1) Continuous batching with adaptive deadlines — improves throughput and reduces per-token cost, minimal impact on p95 when tuned for streaming.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated conversation context — significant token savings for multi-turn flows.
3) Quantization profiles (int8 / mixed-precision) — trade memory for ~1.5-2x cost reduction on GPU-backed inference for compatible models.
4) Model variants — 7B-quantized for cheaper high-throughput paths, 13B or 70B for higher-quality fallbacks; automatic fallback routing by latency and quality policy.
5) Token-level streaming optimizations — smaller initial chunk sizes + aggressive pipelining to reduce first-byte latency.

Open items / next steps:
- Prio: produce a short benchmark matrix (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost/unit) for your representative workload (we requested sample traffic yesterday).
- Internal: Priyom to propose tuning config (batch window, cache TTL, quantization profile) and expected cost delta.
- External: Sophie/Alex to confirm a 2-hour slot for a quick joint benchmark run and share a representative trace file if possible.

Attachments: I've attached a short playbook (redwood-slo-cost-levers-v1.pdf) that summarizes these levers and an example config.

Thanks — I’ll loop Priyom on the follow-up tuning details.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sophie Park <sophie@orionai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and aligns with what we talked about. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 200ms p95 token latency is for user-visible tokens after the first server-side token is generated. We care most about first-byte and steady-state token delivery.
- For concurrency, the 50 concurrent live sessions assume ~2 requests/min per session on average; bursts happen when we run promotions.
- Cost target: we don't have an absolute $/token number to share publicly, but we need relative savings versus our current provider and a model that lets us scale to 5M monthly tokens without linear cost blow-up.

We can do a benchmark run this Thursday 10:00–12:00 PT. I'll upload the sample trace to the Drive link and share credentials for a small test bucket.

Also, can Priyom include recommended model variants and rough expected cost multipliers (e.g., 7B-quantized ~0.4x cost vs 13B-fp16)? That will help our procurement team short-list.

Appreciate the attachment — will review.

—
Sophie Park
Head of Product, Orion AI
Sophie@orionai.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Park <sophie@orionai.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & next steps

Thanks — jumping in with the technical plan for the Thursday benchmark and an initial set of recommended levers. I'll keep the suggestions pragmatic so procurement can map cost estimates.

Planned benchmark (Thursday 10:00–11:30 PT)
- Workload: replay of your provided trace (avg 60 tokens/response, 300 req/min target, sustained 50 concurrent).
- Metrics we’ll capture: first-byte latency, per-token latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens for each config.
- Configs to test: 
  A) Baseline: 13B fp16, no batching (low-latency single-instance)
  B) Continuous batching + 13B fp16 (optimize batch window to hit token p95 target)
  C) 7B int8-quantized + continuous batching (lower-cost, higher throughput)
  D) Hybrid routing: 7B-quantized for 90% traffic, 13B-fp16 fallback for high-latency/complex requests
  E) Cache-enabled variants: same as B/C with prefix/KV cache (TTL tuned to your 15–30s conversation window)

Recommended levers with expected impact (rough estimates):
- Continuous batching (careful tuning): 20–40% cost reduction, small p95 increase if batch windows are too large. Goal: batch window <= 10–15ms to keep streaming p95 within 200–250ms.
- Prefix/KV caching on common system prompts & user history: 15–30% token savings for multi-turn flows.
- 7B int8 quantization: ~0.35–0.5x cost vs 13B fp16 in practice (depends on model ops); expect slightly higher token latency variance but large cost savings.
- Hybrid routing by policy: preserves UX for hard cases while reducing overall cost ~25% depending on routing threshold.
- Streaming pipelining (smaller first-chunk + parallel decode): 50–100ms improvement in first-byte latency in some cases.

What I need from you before Thursday:
- Confirm test window (Sophie confirmed 10:00–11:30 PT).
- Provide the sample trace (or grant Drive access) and a small list of 10 representative long-context examples (8k tokens).
- Any hard constraints on acceptable p99 or error budget so we can tune fallbacks appropriately.

I'll attach a small config template (I’ll paste it into the Drive doc) and a short runbook for the benchmark. After the run we'll produce a one-page matrix with measured latency/cost for each config and a recommended production rollout plan (canary percentages, autoscale tweaks, cache TTLs, quantization profile).

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Perfect — confirm the Thursday slot. I've uploaded the trace to the Drive link and added the 10 long-context examples in a folder called "benchmark-samples". Alex will share the test-bucket credentials by EOD.

For the procurement mapping: rough preference is 7B-int8 for baseline (cost) with a hybrid 13B-fp16 fallback; happy to see the measured multipliers during the run. For error budget, we can tolerate up to 1% request-level failures during the benchmark but want p99 to be under 1s if possible.

See you Thursday.

—
Sophie
